neighbours.label: deferring to tradition, the crowd or the majority as the reason to believe or do something (the word that names the authority: ' tradition', ' group', ' majority', 'this way'), as opposed to the same words in neutral use
fire: Their only defense of the rule was an appeal to tradition.
Teenagers worry so much about agreeing with the group that they stop thinking.
She told the elders that nothing should change merely because of tradition.
Most people simply accept whatever the majority thinks is right.
Our boss rejects every idea because it has always been done this way.
He warned against the tyranny of the majority over lone dissenters.
Unthinking loyalty to the group can silence a person's conscience.
Old guard critics revere tradition and distrust anything new.
quiet: Their village has a charming spring tradition of painted eggs.
Teenagers on the hike lost sight of the group near the waterfall.
She told the elders that the tradition of the harvest dance dates to 1800.
Most seats in the hall went to the majority of late arrivals.
Our boss drives to work every day along this way past the mill.
He sold the majority of his shares for a small profit.
A small group of friends rented a cabin by the sea.
Old family recipes are a tradition at the Christmas table.

short: deferring to tradition or the crowd
